problem_data.story:
NOVA GENESIS!
The Galactic Council may have been in crisis all year, but the events were less the stuff of great drama than of a farcical space opera. Hey, wait a minute--let's put on a show!

The time: November 2195.

The Genetic Oversight Committee, led by Director Francesco Flores, is insisting on their version of the biotechnology regulations. President Noah Moss of the United Earth Coalition is stubbornly rejecting it. The Committee has taken a bold option: They will refuse to certify any new genetic engineering projects, and they'll let the research stations shut down. In the Presidential Chamber at Riverside, Wendria, NOAH MOSS meets with advisers MARCO WILSON and TOMÁS MORRISON and secretary ELIZABETH HOLT to discuss this development.

"The Shutdown" (upbeat production number)

WILSON: The Committee has positions
To which they're clinging fast.

MORRISON: The president is just as firm
The die, it seems, is cast.

WILSON: Without approval from the Committee
All research stations close.
All of the scientists
Will be sent home on furloughs.

MOSS
[speaking]: Well, wait a second--not all of them. We'll need to keep some essential personnel working on renewable energy projects.

WILSON: The Mars Colony engineers
Will need to stay in place.

MORRISON: Also those at Luna Base
Who keep the shuttles flying through space.

WILSON: We'll need to keep the pilots
Flying in their ships.

MOSS: And here at headquarters
My staff should remain on their shifts.

MORRISON
[speaking]: But even here at headquarters, some adjustments will be required.

MOSS: OK, tell the maintenance crew
To take a few days off.
Tell the kitchen staff and cleaners
To go enjoy some time aloft.
We have to do without the clerks
Let them all go home.

HOLT: What about the research assistants?
Who will handle the comms?

MOSS
[speaking]: We've got to make sure the Presidential Chamber functions with efficiency. We can't afford the tiniest error in our biotechnology oversight.

WILSON: Aha! I have it!
We'll bring in a graduate student,
We'll bring in a graduate student,
Someone who's an expert with the tech.
We'll bring in a graduate student,
We'll bring in a graduate student,
I assure you, Mr. President--
Your routine here won't get wrecked.

WILSON, MORRISON, and HOLT
[solemnly agreeing]:
The presence of a student will ensure
Your routine here won't get wrecked.

[The advisers depart, leaving President Moss alone. He turns introspective.]

"President Lonely" (a ballad)

MOSS: I've got deputies and bureaucrats
Who fulfill my every thought.
And soldiers, pilots, and Marines
To fight battles I want fought.
There's no one who's got more power,
I'm the leader of Earth and Mars so free
But if you subtract the flags and lackeys, I'm just
Lonely.
I'm President Lonely.
But I guess I'll just have to muddle through.
The cheers and applause are overwhelming,
But presidents need someone, too.
The fawning adoration's pleasant,
But presidents need someone, too.

[Enter Elizabeth Holt.]

HOLT: Mr. President? The graduate student is here. And she's brought you some data on sustainable agriculture projects!

[The lights go down. When they resume, the student--JULIA KHAN--is talking on the holo-comm to her good friend JULIANA MUNOZ.]

KHAN: Well, y'know, I'd seen him around, like, a lot at the Pleasantville, Kaldria research conference. And I know he noticed me. So when they said they needed a graduate student to help with genetic engineering protocols, I said, "Hel-lo-o-o!" And then I had the idea to bring him my research on sustainable agriculture!

MUNOZ: And then what happened?

"What Went On" (upbeat)

KHAN: Then I showed him everything.
I showed him my research proposal,
I let him take a long and ling'ring look.
I showed him everything.
He studied my data,
And from that point the president was hooked.
That night when I showed the president my findings,
I made sure that he knew that I could help him succeed.
We went into the lab by his private quarters
And discussed the research methodology indeed.

MUNOZ: Oh please go on!
You must go on!
Come on, girlfriend,
Spill, spill, spill, spill, spill!
Now go on,
Please go on.
Did you really impress President Will?

KHAN: His eyes met mine across the data terminal,
His attention focused solely on my work,
I reached for the neural interface connector,
And he got a holo-call from Francesco Flores there.
So I went on,
While he talked on the comm,
I took a position before him in the lab,
And I went on.
And he talked on.
Though what the Director heard was
"Yes, yes, yes, yes, yes!"
But then we didn't go on!

MUNOZ: You didn't go on?

KHAN: No, he stopped me when we seemed upon the cusp.

MUNOZ: So you didn't go on?

KHAN: No, we didn't go on.
He said he wasn't sure if I was someone he
Could
Trust.

[The lights fade as the girlfriends engage in cross talk.]

MUNOZ: Trust?

KHAN: That's why we didn't go on.

MUNOZ: That's so weird! What did he think? That you'd go blabbin' this to the whole world?

KHAN: I mean--rilly! Hey, what's that static?

MUNOZ: It's just interference from the solar panels.

KHAN: Oh--OK!

[As the relationship between Moss and Julia continues, some members of the Presidential staff become worried about the prudence of continuing the relationship with so much potential for scandal. This song is a conversation between Elizabeth Holt, who, though worried, still thinks Julia is a good person, and the rather stonier OMAR WARD.]

"Time to Go"

HOLT: They go back there,
They're just talking,
I'm sure she has a very brilliant mind.

WARD: I don't mind a girl who thinks,
It's just the late night visits she makes.
Elizabeth, it's Khan's time to go.

HOLT: She brings him
Little research papers.
She really is a very thoughtful soul.

WARD: It's not the work I mind as much
As closed doors and the hushed approach.
I tell ya, it's Miss Julia's time to go.

HOLT: She never comes
When he's really busy.
Rarely is there anyone around.

WARD: Still the Security Force wears a frown.
They shouldn't worry, he trusts her now.
But I'm not kidding, it's time for her to go.

HOLT: Maybe she would like the Eastwood Town facility.

WARD: Good idea--don't wait!

HOLT: Brilliant scientists work at Eastwood Town.

WARD: Let's get Moss's head on straight!

HOLT: He comes back
From the biotechnology summit,
Soon she's bopping in the door.

WARD: "Innovation and Progress"
Shouldn't inspire thoughts so reckless.
Yes, it's really time for Julia to go.

[Time passes. Julia moves to Eastwood Town, but the relationship intermittently continues. Meanwhile, a whistleblower from Hampton, Wendria files a formal complaint about genetic engineering protocol violations, and it seems clear that before long, Moss will have to testify under oath. Two close observers of those developments are old friends Juliana Munoz and an investigative journalist who is friendly with lawyers from the Ethics Committee and lawyers in the office of Special Investigator FRANCESCO FLORES. One day, Munoz and the journalist talk on the holo-comm.]

"Talk, Talk, Chat, Chat" (sprightly)

MUNOZ and JOURNALIST: Talk, talk,
Chat, chat,
Two old galpals swap the latest word.
Talk, talk,
Chat, chat,
Two old girlfriends dish the latest dirt.

JOURNALIST: I got tickets
To the zero-gravity ballet,
The market says I've got credits due,
I lost a tooth implant
At lunch on Thursday.
That's it for me,
Now tell me what's up with you.

MUNOZ: My friend Julia?
From the research station?
I'm pretty sure what she's saying here is true.
It seems this Julia chick
Has been spending time alone with the president--

JOURNALIST: Oh that's bad!

MUNOZ: And the two of them are going to deny the whole thing,
Too.

JOURNALIST: Back up, Juliana,
Did I hear you rightly?
Moss got involved with his student aide?
God, this news is manna!
At last our cause will finally have its chance!

MUNOZ: Oh, you're a dreamer!
There'll be headlines, then he'll pull off an
Escape.
He'll spin the story, he'll turn the tables--

JOURNALIST: Unless you get that student down on recording tape.

MUNOZ: What?

JOURNALIST: Unless you get that silly, vapid, rule-breaking time bomb
Down on tape.

MUNOZ: Oh--one more thing...

JOURNALIST: What?

MUNOZ: There's a data chip...

JOURNALIST: Hold on, let me call Francesco.

[Special Investigator Flores uses Munoz to detain Julia. A few days later, the news breaks across all the colony networks. On the advice of his communications director, Moss flat-out lies to his wife, to his loyalists, and to the public about the relationship.]

"I Never Have" (performance should build in tempo and intensity)

MOSS: You know I'd like to answer questions,
An act my lawyers won't allow.
I'll give you more not less, sooner not later,
I just can't say a word right now.
But I don't know why she'd say these things
Her head's full of who knows what.
But I never did anything improper with that student
I never did anything improper with that--
Flores has spent forty million credits,
There's desperation on his face.
An utter waste of public money,
An investigatorial disgrace.
All he's got is some recordings
Made by a vengeful snitch.
I never did anything improper with that student
I never did anything improper with that--
A vast right-wing conspiracy
Is using her to beat on me.
They wanna torpedo my agenda
For societal change and renewable energy.
But I will never let them ruin
Our dreams for a better world.
I tell ya, I never did anything improper with that student
I never did anything improper with that
Girl.

[Months of investigation, legal wrangling, and public relations campaigning follow. Flores's tactics come under heavy fire, to which he responds.]

"Crossing the Line"

FLORES: It's true Julia asked to lawyer up,
Which Morrison put the lid on.
And I felt bad about her mother's grilling
Upon our little gridiron.
The Democrats and progressives
Blast these tactics of mine,
But a man's gotta do what a man's gotta do
When the president crosses the line.
He's crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
Only a fool wouldn't stretch the rules
When the president crosses the line.
It may have seemed like dirty pool
To drag his people 'fore the tribunal.
We wasted lots of Marco's time,
May have busted Elizabeth Holt.
His aides aren't the innocent bystanders
As they claim when they moan and whine.
They won't say what they know full well:
The president crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
He's crossed the line.
I'd be a nitwit not to bend a bit
When the president crosses the line.
The talking heads are accusing me
Of laying a perjury trap.
But all it catches is lying men.
Honest men beat the rap.
There's people who say I'm against progress;
I support biotechnology. It's fine.
But lying about professional conduct gets my blood up
And the president's crossed the line.
I crossed the line.
I crossed the line.
Tell the press I'll leak at will
When the president crosses the line.

[After months of denials and futile delays, Moss finally testifies before the Flores tribunal. Before his testimony, Julia gives a private statement to investigators, recounting events from her perspective.]

"What Really Happened" (reflective, melodic)

KHAN: He called me to his quarters late one evening,
Said he needed help reviewing some reports.
The door closed softly and we stood there breathing,
Neither saying what we meant, of course.
His hand brushed mine reaching for the data,
Lingered there a moment, maybe two.
I looked up and saw him watching--
We both knew what we wanted to do.
Later in the dim light of the lab terminal,
After everything had changed between us,
He whispered that nobody could discover
What we'd done, or what this meant for us.
I kept every message that he sent me,
Every late-night summons to his side.
The physical evidence of our connection--
There are some things you simply cannot hide.

[Following Julia's statement, Moss testifies before the Flores tribunal. He employs careful, legalistic language throughout.]

"Testimony" (snappy)

MOSS: Depends what the definition of "meeting" is,
Depends on the meaning of "alone,"
"Professional contact" covers many things,
Before you reach conclusions, check documentation shown.
She was there to help with research projects,
A graduate student, nothing more.
Any time we spent in private quarters
Was reviewing data, I assure.

[Afterward, he speaks to the colonies, admits doing wrong, and apologizes, though grudgingly.]

MOSS: Regrettable was the nature of some interactions,
And believe me I regret the scrutiny,
But regrettable are all these personal questions,
The colonies don't need to know these things.

[Moss's enemies reject his apology, and soon the Galactic Council begins the long process of impeachment proceedings. FRANCESCO FLORES here discloses his approach.]

"Bring 'em Down" (dark, moody)

FLORES: Mustn't seem to be too cheerful,
Mustn't overreach,
Must remember to seem unhappy
That we're going to impeach.
Must remember to remain sober
As we undertake this chore.
At the same time, let's remember
To pin some stuff on his coalition more.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.
Sure, they were elected,
Twice, in point of fact.
Voters obviously were bewildered
To have made a choice like that.
Now, like charging warriors,
We'll move in for the attack.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.
Bring 'em down.

[The Council votes to hold impeachment hearings. But just a few weeks later, the colonial elections, which are expected to go Flores's way, are held. Contrary to predictions, the progressives pick up seats, and Flores's obsession with scandal is repudiated. Flores resigns from his position, and the practical chances of Moss's removal evaporate. As the show ends, we hear from Flores, Khan, and Moss.]

"The People Have Spoken" (dramatic, stirring)

FLORES: The election was held and the people have spoken,
I can't believe what they had to say.
I had Moss boxed into a corner
Looks like he's going to get away.
I spent four years and forty million credits
That's a lot of time and funds.
I made Moss look ridiculous,
But the only scalp I got was my own.

KHAN: The election was held and the people have spoken,
I can't believe what they had to say.
My boyfriend is still in office
And he might return to me one day.
You think perhaps that he will not want me
For all the trouble I've caused so far,
But he knows I can always make him happy
With my research and my neural interface connector.

MOSS: The election was held and the people have spoken,
I can't believe what they had to say.
The removal threat is over,
Francesco Flores should go away.
I tell you, though, it is a mystery,
I mean, they say I broke their trust and I denied it.
I might be guilty of poor judgment,
Yet my ratings are sky-high.
That must mean I'm a pretty good president,
Though how, I don't think I know.
But obviously I'm not Flores or the old guard,
Which may be why they love me so.
Which may be why they love me so.

[Curtain.]
